problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a critical inspection circuit across eight regional warehouses, each positioned at distinct geographical sites:

Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (139,38)  
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at grid reference (26,152)  
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (124,37)  
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at grid reference (144,103)  
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (163,174)  
Warehouse Zeta: Positioned at grid reference (108,133)  
Warehouse Eta: Positioned at grid reference (126,173)  
Warehouse Theta: Positioned at grid reference (82,127)

The travel distances between any two warehouses, measured in kilometers along existing transport links, are precisely defined as follows:

Alpha to Gamma: 15.0 km  
Alpha to Delta: 65.2 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 138.1 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 99.9 km  
Alpha to Eta: 135.6 km  
Alpha to Theta: 105.7 km  
Beta to Gamma: 151.1 km  
Beta to Delta: 127.8 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 138.8 km  
Beta to Zeta: 84.2 km  
Beta to Eta: 102.2 km  
Beta to Theta: 61.3 km  
Gamma to Delta: 69.0 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 142.4 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 97.3 km  
Gamma to Eta: 136.0 km  
Gamma to Theta: 99.3 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 73.5 km  
Delta to Zeta: 46.9 km  
Delta to Eta: 72.3 km  
Delta to Theta: 66.5 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 68.6 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 37.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 93.6 km  
Zeta to Eta: 43.9 km  
Zeta to Theta: 26.7 km  
Eta to Theta: 63.7 km

Due to infrastructural limitations, no direct transport corridor exists between Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta. Furthermore, a mandatory routing regulation stipulates that exactly one of two specified corridors must be incorporated into the final circuit: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop inspection tour, visiting each warehouse exactly once before returning to the origin, thereby minimizing the total travel distance.
